concepts.learning_objective: Describe a point as a precise location with no length, breadth or height.
Identify a line segment as the shortest path between two end points and name it.
Recognise that a line extends endlessly both ways and that two points determine a unique line.
Describe a ray as a part of a line with one starting point going endlessly in one direction.
Name a ray correctly using its starting point first and any other point on it.
Identify the vertex and arms of an angle formed by two rays with a common starting point.
Name angles using three letters with the vertex as the middle letter.
Explain the size of an angle as the amount of turn about the vertex.
Compare two angles by superimposing them with their vertices overlapping.
Compare angles without superimposition using a transparent circle centred at the vertex.
Recognise that the size of an angle does not depend on the lengths of its arms.
Relate straight and right angles to half and quarter turns.
Identify perpendicular lines as lines meeting at right angles and justify right angles made by folding.
Classify angles as acute or obtuse by comparing them with a right angle.
Use the fact that a full turn is 360 degrees to find measures of angles.
Read and draw angles correctly with a protractor.
Explain bisecting an angle and find angles made by repeated halving.

topics.title: Types of angles and their measures

concepts.learning_objective: Classify angles as acute, right, obtuse, straight or reflex from their degree measures.
Find the measure of a reflex angle from the angle on the other side.
Find an unknown angle using the fact that a straight angle measures 180 degrees.
